title: ServeFlow weekly sync — prep & action tracker (Amelia Chen)
content:
Purpose: quick alignment for weekly ServeFlow sync. Keep this short — agenda + 15–20m deep dives, then 10m action review.

Context: recent tail-latency spike on 3/8 after the batcher changes; Diego rolled back the experiment and we saw improvement. We need a safe rollout plan and follow-ups on observability to catch regressions sooner. Also want to finalize the console trace change for per-model routing policy visibility.

Goals for this meeting:
- Agree on rollout strategy for the adaptive batcher (canary size, metrics for rollback).
- Decide ownership and timeline for new trace fields in Console UI API.
- Quick status on KV cache priming experiments and SLO impact.
- Capture concrete action items and owners.

Proposed agenda (30m):
1) Quick status (5m) — Diego
   - Short recap of rollback and current baseline latency/throughput numbers.
   - Any outstanding infra alerts?
2) Batcher rollout plan (10m) — Amelia + Arjun
   - Canary cohorts: 5% low-latency apps, 2% high-throughput tenants.
   - Metric gates: p95 token latency, tail failure rate, CPU GPU utilization, dropped requests.
   - Rollout cadence: 6h -> 24h -> 3d with automated rollback if metric gate trips.
3) Console trace fields (6m) — Lena
   - Add model_variant, route_policy, and batcher_config into trace event.
   - Backwards-compatible schema: new optional keys.
4) KV cache priming update (5m) — Arjun
   - Short experiment results: priming reduced average token compute by ~7% for sequence-heavy jobs.
5) Action review / next steps (4m) — Amelia

Talking points / open questions to raise:
- How should we set rollback thresholds for multi-tenant signals (tenant-level vs cluster-level)?
- Is the current tracing ingest capacity sufficient for the added fields? Is there a cost impact?
- Any objections to canary cohort composition (5% low-latency, 2% high-throughput)?
- Does Support need a pre-brief for the rollout window?

Notes to self (scratch ideas):
- Consider a lightweight canary dashboard widget filtered by tenant tag and SLO bucket.
- If priming shows stable wins, add an automatic priming job into the pre-warm pipeline with a toggle.
- Draft a short support playbook for rollback and postmortem owners.

Action items (tracked, simple format):
1) Diego Ramos — "Collect baseline metrics and post-rollback comparison table" — due 2026-03-13
2) Amelia Chen — "Draft canary rollout plan doc & metric gates; include abort criteria" — due 2026-03-14 (link to PR in linked artifacts when ready)
3) Lena Wu — "Update Console trace API spec and mock UI change; estimate ingest cost impact" — due 2026-03-16
4) Arjun Patel — "Run extended KV priming for 48h on warm cohort; capture cost delta" — due 2026-03-15
5) Support (cc: Priya) — "Prepare a one-pager with rollback contact and customer-facing messaging" — due 2026-03-14
6) Amelia Chen + Diego Ramos — "Set up canary dashboard widget & alert (p95 increase > 20% triggers)" — due 2026-03-15

Follow-up plan:
- After canary doc is posted, schedule a 20m canary kickoff with SRE + Console + Support (target: 2026-03-17).
- If canary passes 72h, plan gradual ramp with checkpoints and a retrospective session.

Misc links to paste into the doc during prep:
- EXPERIMENT: batcher-v2 rollback notes: https://jira.internal.redwood/INF-2378
- ServeFlow PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serveflow/pull/142
- Console trace schema doc (placeholder): confluence/internal/serveflow-trace-schema

Quick calendar blurb to copy into the invite:
"Purpose: brief alignment on adaptive batcher rollout, console trace fields, and KV priming results. Goal is to agree on canary plan and owners. Expect 30 minutes; bring data and any support constraints.

If you can't make it, drop brief notes in this doc or flag blockers in Slack (#serveflow)."

End of notes.
